How Nav mode, Ctrl and app shortcuts work together

Nav mode turns letter keys into arrows, selection and shortcut keys. Results can differ by app. Some apps understand Android text actions, and others only react to real Ctrl shortcuts.
Double-tap Ctrl Double-tap Ctrl to turn Nav mode on. Letters then do their Nav mode job until you leave Nav mode. This is handy for arrows, Page up and Page down, Escape, Tab and selecting text without holding Ctrl.
Ctrl-hold navigation When this is off, holding Ctrl sends normal Ctrl shortcuts to the app, so Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I or Ctrl+Z work in editors.
When this is on, holding Ctrl uses the Nav mode keys below instead.
Action or Ctrl shortcut Actions such as Copy, Paste, Cut, Select all and Undo are sent as Android text actions. They work in most text fields, but not every app supports every action.
Choose Ctrl shortcut when an app expects a real shortcut. For example, setting I to Ctrl shortcut sends Ctrl+I, so editors such as Google Docs make text italic. Undo can also be a Ctrl shortcut if an app handles Ctrl+Z better.
Changing keys Tap a key below to choose what it does: a key, an action, a Ctrl shortcut or nothing. Use this to fix conflicts in a specific app without changing everything else.
